title: B3 BUILD (control-plane): conflict-detection pass - precedent.py conflicts subcommand + tests
description: Roadmap Part II deliverable 4: a conflict-detection pass that flags contradictory active precedents. Per coordinator decision D6 it is an ON-DEMAND CLI pass modelled on lock.py sweep and blackboard.py expire-claims - never a hook, never a hard gate, identical behavior for Claude, Codex, Gemini and human (engine parity is the invariant; hooks are Claude-side sugar - ORCHESTRATION.md:193-196). Extends .harness/bin/precedent.py, which T-340 already shipped and a verifier already accepted; acquire its lock before writing. Sibling task T-343 runs in parallel and does not touch this file.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS: the conflicts subcommand inside .harness/bin/precedent.py (acquire lock.py on it; T-340 is done, so there is no race) and a NEW test file .harness/tests/test_precedent_conflicts.py. Writing its own test file is deliberate: it never races T-340's .harness/tests/test_precedent.py, and the acceptance glob test_precedent*.py discovers both. Do NOT write PRECEDENT.md (T-341/T-345), do NOT publish live seed records (T-343), do NOT write state.json or blackboard.json.

DETECTORS, at minimum: (1) two ACTIVE records whose ratio decisions contradict on the same subject key; (2) an active record citing an OVERRULED record as binding support; (3) an overruling performed by a LOWER authority tier than the tier that issued the overruled record (illegitimate overruling per D4); (4) scope-condition overlap - two active records of the same tier claiming the same scope with different ratios; (5) DANGLING CITATIONS - a PR-NNN or T-xxx reference that does not resolve. Detector 5 is the class the harness's own live integrity gap belongs to (P-023 applied in code at .harness/bin/blackboard.py:470 and in prose at ORCHESTRATION.md:58 but absent from state.json evolution.accepted_mutations - see .harness/context-brief-precedent-layer.md section 2.4 and state.json:791).

EXIT-CODE CONTRACT per T-339: 0 when no conflicts, a documented nonzero code when conflicts are found (so a verifier or a future CI step can consume it), and a distinct code for usage errors. The pass MUST NOT block, gate or slow any other CLI call, and MUST NOT install a hook.
REPORT FORMAT: every finding names the detector, the records involved by PR-NNN, and the evidence that triggered it - a finding a human cannot check by hand is a false green in disguise.

ALL TESTS use a temporary registry root through the override T-340 shipped; assert that .harness/precedents/ is NOT written during the test run. Include a fixture reproducing the P-023-shaped case (a record whose cited authority does not resolve) and assert the pass flags it. Include a CLEAN control fixture and assert zero findings on it - a detector with no false-positive test is untested.
stdlib only, must run under bare python3 (3.9.6), no new dependencies, no new log file (use harness_common.log_event if an event is warranted).

ACCEPTANCE COMMANDS, exactly (P-025): python3 -m unittest discover -s .harness/tests -p "test_precedent*.py" -v reports a NONZERO executed-test count (quote the Ran N line) and passes - note this now runs BOTH test files; python3 -m py_compile .harness/bin/precedent.py exits 0.
Hand off to role verifier (T-347 replays this adversarially with its own planted conflicts, not your fixtures).

OPEN-QUESTION (for T-345 / T-347, NOT blocking this verdict): citation CYCLES are neither detected nor documented as a limit. I planted a 2-cycle (PR-001 cites PR-002, PR-002 cites PR-001), a SELF-citation (PR-003 cites PR-003) and a 3-cycle (PR-004 -> PR-005 -> PR-006 -> PR-004); every member resolves, so det5 stays silent and the pass reports rc=0, "0 findings across 6 record(s)". Cycles are absent from AC-2's "at minimum" detector list so this is not an AC miss, but grep -i cycle finds nothing in precedent.py or PRECEDENT.md, so the limit is undisclosed rather than accepted. A self-citing record is arguably a real integrity defect: a record cannot be its own authority.

OPEN-QUESTION (for T-345, NOT blocking): detector 4's notion of scope "overlap" is exact string-set intersection, and that proxy is undisclosed. Scope role:worker versus role:worker|verifier at the same tier with directly contradictory ratios yields zero findings. Detector 1's docstring explicitly discloses its own proxy nature (mechanical proxy for "contradict", semantic judgment stays a verifier's job, R-6); detector 4 carries no equivalent note. AC-2 item 4's own wording is "claiming the same scope", which exact matching satisfies, so this is a documentation gap rather than a spec violation.
